doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Father a chauffeur; Japanese couples displace black chauffeurs
summary: His father was a chauffeur and mother a housewife; in the Depression Japanese couples took over household service jobs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And that was considered to be a pretty good job.
I was going to ask what your parents did for a living.

Yeah. And my mother, she was a housewife, she stayed home. And what happened, see most of the chauffeurs, they hired colored chauffeurs. A large percentage of the chauffeurs were colored chauffeurs. That was considered a good job. In later years, especially during the depression, see what happened, a lot of oriental people came in, the Japanese, and they would hire the husband and wife. They would stay on the premises. The wife would do the cooking and the house cleaning and the husband would do the gardening and general clean up, butlering, and chauffeur. So that was during the depression.
So African-American chauffeurs found themselves out of work?
